purpose: Falsify the naive hypothesis that a familiarity threshold calibrated only for known-class coverage is sufficient for open-set safety.

setup.acceptance_score: minimum Euclidean distance to known prototype

falsified_claim: Known-distribution calibration of prototype distance is by itself sufficient to guarantee safe unknown rejection under user-specific distribution shift.
interpretation: The same threshold can preserve approximately 95% known acceptance while catastrophically accepting a shifted semantically-unknown population that overlaps the known embedding neighborhood. This synthetic result does not quantify FRANK's real false-familiarity rate; it establishes only a counterexample to the naive guarantee.
architecture_consequence: Calibration must carry explicit validity/shift assumptions and cannot become semantic authority. Unknown-risk evidence, drift/validity state, and escalation remain mandatory.
next_real_test: Extend MVC-E5 with near-unknown user-specific confusers, distribution-shift slices, calibration-version invalidation and candidate-vs-current risk receipts on real frozen Retina embeddings.
